messages.author: 3314d7ad28eab19e
messages.subject: DSM for point count data
parts:
Hi all,

I'm wondering if I can develop a DSM for point count data. I know it is possible to estimate the detection function, and it would appear that one could manipulate the data in some way as to create segmented areas using the point counts. For example: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/distance-sampling/dsm$20point$20count%7Csort:relevance/distance-sampling/dG-YCu9EV6w/FU8KF7q_BwAJ. My only idea was to generate a grid around the observation points and create the necessary fields for the segment.data object. Would it be a bad idea to try this? Are there other options?

Thanks & best regards,
Shawn

messages.author: 1fb54f491646a589
messages.subject: RE: [distance-sampling] DSM for point count data
parts:
Shawn, there is no need to create segmented areas for point data.  Methods for DSM for point data are outlined in

 

Hedley, S.L., Buckland, S.T. and Borchers, D.L. 2004.  Spatial distance sampling models.  In Advanced Distance Sampling, pp48-70.  S.T. Buckland, D.R. Anderson, K.P. Burnham, J.L. Laake, D.L. Borchers and L. Thomas (eds).  Oxford University Press, Oxford.

 

And there is some discussion of modelling options in section 3 of

 

Buckland, S.T., Oedekoven, C.S. and Borchers, D.L. 2016.  Model-based distance sampling.  Journal of Agricultural, Biological and Environmental Statistics 21, 58-75.

 

Steve Buckland

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM for point count data
parts:
Hi Guillaume, Eric, and others,

I just wanted to thank you for your responses to my question. Thanks especially to Guillaume for posting an example! I've been able to work this out with my survey data and it is looking promising. I'm looking forward to seeing more on this topic, as Eric had indicated in a previous post.

One question I have is this: how worried should we be if the truncated distances of the point surveys overlap each other in some cases? It seems like DSMs do a pretty good job of handling non-independence of point surveys by modeling the observed abundance estimates as a function of spatial covariates. In addition, I see little evidence of residual spatial autocorrelation after fitting DSMs to the data. Nonetheless, I could benefit from a better understanding of how this might affect results.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM for point count data
parts:
Shawn

Happy to hear Guillaume's analysis was of use to you.  He deserves all the credit.

I can point you to some literature on your first point, but not to your second point.  In 2006 Prof Buckland published a paper in The Auk on conventional analysis of point transect sampling.  As part of that paper, he conducted a simulation study investigating (among other things) the effect of overlap of points such that most birds were detected from >1 point.  A quote from the results:

"For population 2, there was severe overlap between plots, so that most birds in the study area were detected more than once. On average, there were 356 detections from a population of 225 birds, of which only 100 birds were within the central 1-km square that was surveyed. Nevertheless, there was almost no bias in estimated bird density: true density was one bird ha–1, and the mean of the 1,000 estimated densities
was 1.0056 ± 0.0026 birds ha–1 (mean ± SE). There was also only mild underestimation of the standard error: true standard error (estimated by
the standard deviation of the 1,000 population size estimates) was 0.0815, whereas the mean of the 1,000 analytic standard errors was 0.0750."
